Remark Prior art: q-Ward identities with separate unit-circle and real-q solutions. Belaey, Mertens and Papalini solve the q-Ward identities for the two-point function on the quantum disk [belaey2025, \S 2.1, pp. 7--8]. The solution depends on the range of q. For q = e^{i\pi b} on the unit circle it is the analytic continuation of their eq. (2.19) to non-integer weight; for 0 < q < 1 it is a convergent infinite product. In both regimes the correlator shows q-deformed hyperbolic disk isometries.

This is an external case, alongside the comparison with canonical programmes, of one q-symmetry having different solutions on the unit circle and on the real line, which is also how QOU separates root-of-unity and real-q evaluations. It is a structural parallel only. The paper's real range is 0 < q < 1, not q_0 > 1, and its b is not checked against the b of the Faddeev quantum dilogarithm used in the corpus, so it is not evidence for any QOU identification.
conj:lqg-entropy-qdim-partition-pole:
Conjecture Horizon entropy as the q-dimension partition-function pole. The LQG horizon-entropy state count admits a QOU recasting. The analytic Laplace count becomes an algebraic partition-function pole.

Conjecture. Let the horizon be punctured by knot operators, each carrying a non-trivial \mathrm{SU}_q(2) boundary representation V_j of spin j \in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{>0} (j \geq \frac{1}{2}). Define the per-puncture q-dimension partition function

  Z_1(s) \;=\; \sum_{j \in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{>0}} [2j+1]_q \,
  e^{-s\,\tau\!\bigl(C_q(V_j)\bigr)},

where \tau(C_q(V_j)) > 0 is the archimedean image of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Casimir on V_j (excluding the trivial representation j = 0, which imparts zero area and does not puncture the horizon). Then:

  1. Entropy = pole. Because Z_1(s) decreases strictly and continuously from +\infty as s \to 0^+ to 0 as s \to +\infty, the horizon-state generating function \sum_{n\ge0} Z_1(s)^n = (1 - Z_1(s))^{-1} has a unique simple pole at the critical value s_\star = s_\star(q) satisfying Z_1(s_\star) = 1, and the entropy density is s_\star.
  2. Gauss constraint = trace closure. The closed-horizon U(1) Gauss constraint \sum_p m_p = 0 is the trace-closure condition. The closed-link evaluation is a morphism \mathbf{1} \to \mathbf{1}.
  3. Immirzi from criticality. Matching to the Bekenstein–Hawking law S = A/4\ell_p^2 fixes the Barbero–Immirzi parameter as \gamma(q) = s_\star(q)/2\pi. (Fixing \gamma by agreement with the Bekenstein–Hawking law is the procedure of [domagala-lewandowski-2004, \S1]; the exact leading area term that makes the match possible is [meissner2004].)

Scope. This is an algebraic recasting of an established analytic result (the combinatorial state count of [domagala-lewandowski-2004], solved exactly, with a -\tfrac12\ln A correction, in [meissner2004]), not a from-scratch derivation of black-hole entropy. In the classical q \to 1 limit, [2j+1]_1 = 2j+1 recovers the classical \mathrm{SU}(2) puncture sum, so the leading \gamma is the q \to 1 value and is q_0-independent. True q_0-dependence enters through the q-deformed quantum dimensions [2j+1]_{q_0} and q-Casimir eigenvalues \tau(C_{q_0}(V_j)), which determine s_\star(q_0) and hence \gamma(q_0) = s_\star(q_0)/2\pi.
rem:sym2-adjoint-spin-two-gauge-not-lore:
Remark The spin-2 summand of \mathrm{Sym}^2(V_1) is gauge spin, not spacetime spin. By the traceless symmetric square proposition, the adjoint V_1 of the gauge group G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2) of the emergence theorem satisfies \mathrm{Sym}^2(V_1) \ominus V_0 \cong V_2, the spin-2 object of dimension 5. A symmetric traceless tensor of spin 2 is the shape of a graviton, so the scope of this result needs stating.

Gauge spin and spacetime spin. The proposition is representation theory of the gauge group \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau). "Spin 2" there means that V_2 is the five-dimensional simple representation of that group. A graviton is a massless particle of helicity \pm 2, that is, a representation of the Poincaré group whose field is a symmetric rank-2 tensor of the Lorentz group \mathrm{SO}(3,1). The two statements concern different groups. No proved statement of the corpus identifies \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) with, or maps it onto, a spacetime rotation or Lorentz group, and none is used here. The closest text is the spatial-isotropy condition in the preamble to Bring's surface, which relates the spatial rotation algebra \mathfrak{so}(3) to Reeb degrees of the adjoint involution. That condition is a motivating requirement on the choice of surface, not a theorem, and it concerns spatial rotations only, not the Lorentz group.

A reading of V_2 as a graviton would therefore need two further results:

  1. a homomorphism from \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) to the spacetime Lorentz group under which the gauge adjoint V_1 transforms as a spacetime vector;
  2. a reason why the symmetric traceless tensor built from V_1, rather than from a spacetime vector representation, carries the metric fluctuation.

What this remark does not claim. It makes no claim that any object of \mathbf{C} is a graviton, no claim about a coupling, a mass or a field equation, and no empirical prediction.

whose image in H_3(q) is the longest basis element T_{w_0}. Its closure is the positive Hopf link: the word permutes the three strands by a transposition, so the closure has two components, with linking number +1.

def:positron-knot:
Definition Positron. The positron is the conjugate of the electron word, with every crossing reversed:

  e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} \in B_3 .

Its closure is the negative Hopf link. It serves as the antiparticle of the electron.

Like the electron, environment distinguishes the positron from its quark counterpart (the down quark). Reversing every crossing shifts the Coulomb charge from Q = -1 to Q = +1.

In the Reeb flow, crossing reversal corresponds to reversing time. The positron thus represents an electron traveling backward in time, recovering the Feynman–Stueckelberg interpretation.
def:neutrino-knot:
Definition Neutrino. The neutrino corresponds to the unknot K_{0_1}.

  \nu =  K_{0_1} \qquad \text{(unknot, circle ○)}

The unknot has Seifert genus 0, crossing number 0, and a trivial Skein polynomial J_\nu(q) = 1. It contributes no hyperbolic volume and thus carries no topological mass. Instead, neutrino mass arises entirely from vacuum drag.

The neutrino is drawn as a simple circle.

The unknot dictates the neutrino's physical properties:

  • Zero crossing chirality: The lack of crossings ensures electrical neutrality (Q(\nu) = 0).
  • Trivial braiding: The R-matrix acts as the identity on the unknot. Neutrinos therefore evade the crossing-energy interactions responsible for Coulomb repulsion.
  • Vacuum drag mass: The mass m_\nu \sim \mu_0 \cdot (q - 1) scales with the baseline vacuum drag, vanishing at q = 1.

  \nu^{\sigma} =  T_{1,0}^{\sigma} \qquad \text{(mirror unknot, dashed circle ⊙)}

conj:borromean-quark:
Conjecture Quarks as Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor. Quarks are not fundamental knots. A quark is a neutrino (an unknot) trapped in a color tube of Bring's surface. It links Borromean-style with two other unknots in the exceptional divisor.

The baryon is the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 of three unknots threaded through the color tubes (r, g, b) of the Bring's surface (color tube coordinates), bound by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H:

  \mathfrak{p}
  = 
  \mathcal{B}_3(\nu_r, \nu_g, \nu_b)
   \oplus  \mathcal{L}_H,

where the unknots \nu_r, \nu_g, \nu_b (neutrino) localize in the red, green, and blue color tubes, respectively. The "up" and "down" quark flavours correspond to the crossing orientation of each unknot within the Borromean structure.

Borromean rather than Hopf.

The Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 requires that no two components link, yet all three together remain inseparable. Removing any one component frees the other two. This enforces color confinement. No isolated quark (a single unknot removed from \mathcal{B}_3) can exist. No two-quark bound state (a diquark) is stable. Only the three-quark composite remains confined.

The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H, by contrast, links any two components pairwise. A Hopf chain of three unknots permits diquark states (remove one, and the other two remain linked), contradicting confinement. The two cases are told apart by link-homotopy invariants: three-component links in S^3 are classified up to link homotopy by their pairwise linking numbers and Milnor's triple linking number, and the Borromean rings have all pairwise numbers zero and triple number \pm 1 [dgkmsv2013].

Mass from linking, not from constituents.

The three individual unknots possess zero hyperbolic volume: \mathrm{Vol}(K_{0_1}) = 0. The neutrino mass is near zero. However, the Borromean link possesses a nonzero hyperbolic volume:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3) =  7.32772\ldots

By the topological mass formula \mathfrak{m} = \mathrm{Vol}(K) / \hbar_q^2, the baryon mass derives entirely from the Borromean linking, not from the constituent unknots. This matches the standard QCD result: roughly 99\% of the proton's 938 MeV derives from gluon binding energy, while quark Higgs masses contribute only roughly 10 MeV.

Up and down from crossing orientation.

Within \mathcal{B}_3, the cyclic symmetry of the color tubes relates the three components. The S_3 permutation symmetry acts on the color assignment (r, g, b). Breaking this symmetry into a 2 + 1 partition yields two components with one crossing orientation (up quarks) and one with the reversed orientation (down quark):

  • Up quark (u): Unknot in a color tube with positive crossing orientation within \mathcal{B}_3. It contributes +2/3 to the proton charge.
  • Down quark (d): Unknot in a color tube with negative (reversed) crossing orientation within \mathcal{B}_3. It contributes -1/3 to the proton charge.

The proton \mathfrak{p} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]_p exhibits the 2 + 1 partition: two positive-orientation unknots and one negative. The neutron \mathfrak{n} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}]_p exhibits the 1 + 2 partition.

Crossing orientation is not writhe. The \pm labels denote the exponent sign of the braid generator at each crossing of \mathcal{B}_3 (explicitly, \sigma_i for positive and \sigma_i^{-1} for negative). The generator index i \in \{0, 1\} identifies which adjacent pair of strands crosses, independently of the sign. These crossings occur between distinct strands, not as self-crossings of any single strand. In the standard braid projection, each strand maintains zero self-writhe. The free neutrino remains the same unknot drawn outside any Borromean context. All three pairwise linking numbers vanish (the Brunnian property), while the triple Milnor invariant \bar{\mu}_{123} = \pm 1 encodes confinement.

The exceptional divisor as quark habitat.

Borromean linking occurs in the exceptional divisor of the brane tower, the blow-up locus where the color tubes of Bring's surface meet. The unknots (neutrinos) are spacetime objects. Their Borromean linking is a fiber phenomenon existing exclusively in the exceptional divisor. A free neutrino (an unknot outside a color tube) lacks Borromean partners and acquires no mass from linking.

This framework explains why quarks never appear in isolation. The Borromean structure requires the exceptional divisor. Pulling a quark out of the baryon means extracting an unknot from \mathcal{B}_3. This action unlinks the remaining two components and destroys the baryon. The energy required for this separation exceeds the threshold to create a new quark-antiquark pair (a new Borromean triple). Consequently, the extracted quark immediately re-confines.

The T(2,n) family.

The torus knot/link family T(2,n) on the Bring's surface splits into two parallel ladders. The torus-knot particle spectrum is tabulated in Table: Torus-knot particle spectrum.

  • Odd n: Knots (1 component) yield fermions (matter).
  • Even n: Links (2 components) yield bosons (force carriers).

The gluon is T(2,2), the Hopf link, not T(2,7). The Hopf link has two components that mediate the color interaction between two of the three Borromean unknots. There are \binom{3}{2} = 3 such pairs, yielding eight gluons from the \mathrm{SU}(3) color algebra acting on the three Borromean components.

Consistency with the Skein mass relation.

Under the mass reading of hadron reading of skein generation, the skein resolution of skein generation writes the mass of a hadronic link as a polynomial in unknot and Hopf-link masses. def:Q-value-transition:
Definition \mathcal{Q}_q-Value as Categorical Action Difference. Let \mathcal{N}(Z,N) be the normal form of a nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons, and let \mathfrak{S}_q(\mathcal{N}) be its categorical action (categorical action), which on static rest configurations (\mathcal{L}_1 = 0) coincides with the rest projection of the categorical Hamiltonian in the aether mass chart.   \mathcal{Q}_q
  = 
  \mathfrak{S}_q\bigl(\mathcal{N}(Z,N)\bigr) -
  \mathfrak{S}_q\bigl(\mathcal{N}(Z{+}1,N{-}1)\bigr) -
  \mathfrak{S}_q(e) -
  \mathfrak{S}_q(\bar{\nu}_e),

with \mathfrak{S}_q(\bar{\nu}_e) = 0 since the antineutrino is the unknot. This is the primary definition. It does not assume classical energy conservation, which is the q = 1 limit; the relation between \mathcal{Q}_q and the kinetic energies of the products is the q-anomaly \delta_q treated in Crossing-level decomposition, the q-anomaly, and non-conservation of \mathcal{Q}_q. When q is fixed, Q denotes \mathcal{Q}_q.

Mass-difference form. In the archimedean neutral-atom MeV mass chart the rest Hamiltonian of a nucleus is its mass, and the same transition evaluates as the difference of neutral atomic masses,

  Q = M(Z, N) - M(Z{+}1, N{-}1),
  \qquad
  M(Z, N) = Z m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z m_e - B(Z, N),

where B(Z,N) = -\Delta H_{\mathrm{can}} is the positive binding-energy release at Hecke level k under the Bethe--Weizsäcker emergence conjecture (Seven-term atomic mass formula with q-integer coefficients). Expanding the atomic masses gives Q = m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} - m_e - \bigl(B(Z,N) - B(Z{+}1,N{-}1)\bigr). This is the form in which Q is compared with measured values; it is a chart realisation of -\Delta H_{\mathrm{can}}, not a second definition, and its numerical content is conditional on the conjecture that supplies B.
rem:Q-value-transition-properties:
Remark Crossing-level decomposition, the q-anomaly, and non-conservation of \mathcal{Q}_q. This section develops the Q-value of a nuclear transition. It analyses its precision behaviour, crossing-level decomposition, q-anomaly, and the non-conservation of q-momentum. The q-anomaly breaks classical energy conservation.

This definition is consistent with mass accuracy. If |\Delta M/M| \approx 0.002\%, then Q-values for transitions with Q \gg \Delta M inherit the same precision. For transitions with small Q (e.g. {}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He}, Q = 18.6 keV), catastrophic cancellation amplifies the mass error: \delta Q/Q \approx (M/Q) \times (\delta M/M).

At k = 11: Q(n \to {}^1\mathrm{H}) = 0.782 MeV (0.00\%), Q({}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He}) = 0.01823 MeV (-2.1\%).

Crossing-level decomposition

The parent normal form \mathcal{N}(p,n) and daughter normal form \mathcal{N}(p+1, n-1) differ at exactly |\delta p| crossings. These are the quarks of the converting nucleon. At each changed crossing:

  \Delta \mathfrak{E}_\times
  = 
  \mathfrak{E}_\times^{(\epsilon_{\mathrm{par}})}(q)
  - \mathfrak{E}_\times^{(\epsilon_{\mathrm{dau}})}(q).

For a \mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u} change (\sigma_k^{-1} \to \sigma_k), \Delta \mathfrak{E}_\times = q - q^{-1}. The Q-value is:

  Q
  = 
  \sum_{\text{changed crossings}} \Delta \mathfrak{E}_\times
  -  \mathfrak{S}_q(e).

The unknot has trivial action. Drop \mathfrak{S}_q(\nu^{\sigma}) = 0.

Classical limit and the q-anomaly

Warning. Classical energy conservation is not assumed.

In classical physics, conservation of energy defines the Q-value:

  Q_{\mathrm{classical}}
  = 
  T_e + T_{\nu^{\sigma}} + T_{\mathrm{recoil}}
  \stackrel{?}{=}
  M_{\mathrm{par}} - M_{\mathrm{dau}} - m_e.

This equality uses E_{\mathrm{before}} = E_{\mathrm{after}}. In the q-deformed framework, this conservation law fails because the q-differential does not satisfy d_q^2 = 0:

  d_q f(x) =  \frac{f(qx) - f(x)}{(q-1)x}.
  d_q(f \cdot g) =  (d_q f) \cdot g +  f(qx) \cdot (d_q g).

The q-Leibniz rule has a shift f(qx) rather than f(x). The q-differential of a product is not the sum of differentials. Squaring gives:

  d_q^2  \neq  0 \quad \text{for } q \neq 1.

Corollary: The total q-energy of the products need not equal the total q-energy of the parent. Define the q-anomaly:

  \delta_q
   := 
  Q
  - 
  (T_e + T_{\nu^{\sigma}} + T_{\mathrm{recoil}}).

This anomaly is a genuine physical effect of the q-deformation. It does not vanish in general.

Structure of the q-anomaly

The q-anomaly arises from the non-commutativity of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra. The Skein crossing change converts one quark. The re-reduction to Gröbner--Shirshov normal form introduces R2 moves T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1. Each R2 move shifts the local q-environment:

  q_{\mathrm{eff}} \mapsto q_{\mathrm{eff}} + \Delta q,

where \Delta q \propto \hbar_q^2 = (1 - q^{-1})^2.

The self-deformation produces a net shift:

  \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}
  = 
  \frac{A - 1}{A^2} \cdot \hbar_q^2.

This shift modifies Q at second order:

  Q
  = 
  \underbrace{\Delta \mathfrak{S}_q - \mathfrak{S}_q(e)}_{\text{leading (crossing change)}}
  + 
  \underbrace{\frac{\partial \mathfrak{S}_q}{\partial q} \cdot \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}}_{\delta_q \text{ (q-anomaly)}}.

At q = 1: \delta_q = 0 and Q \to Q_{\mathrm{classical}}. Classical conservation is restored.

At the aether parameter q: \delta_q \neq 0. For tritium (A = 3), \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}} = 2/9 \cdot \hbar_q^2 \approx 0.0022. This gives a correction \delta_q / Q \sim 5\%. This correction brings the tritium half-life prediction from 13 yr to 12.4 yr (observed 12.32 yr).

Q is not conserved

The q-anomaly \delta_q implies that Q is not the sum of kinetic energies. The q-deformation of the vacuum absorbs the missing energy. The effective aether parameter shifts from q to q + \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}.

This is the q-deformed quantum anomaly. The full categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q of the entire system is the conserved quantity:

  \mathfrak{S}_q(\mathrm{par})
  = 
  \mathfrak{S}_{q + \Delta q}(\mathrm{dau})
  + 
  \mathfrak{S}_q(e)
  + 
  \mathfrak{S}_q(\nu^{\sigma})
  + 
  \text{kinetic terms}.

Evaluate the daughter at the shifted q. This is the q-analogue of energy conservation.

q-Momentum

The q-momentum satisfies a similar non-conservation. Classically:

  \vec{p}_{\mathrm{par}} = \vec{p}_{\mathrm{dau}} + \vec{p}_e + \vec{p}_{\nu^{\sigma}}.

In the q-deformed case, the Iwahori--Hecke algebra non-commutativity implies:

  p_q(\mathrm{par})
  = 
  p_q(\mathrm{dau}) + p_q(e) + p_q(\nu^{\sigma})
  +

where \delta p_q \propto \hbar_q is a q-anomaly in momentum. This is the braid-group analogue of the quantum anomaly in gauge theories.

Definition Breit--Wheeler pair production (categorical). The Breit--Wheeler process models categorical pair production, \gamma\gamma \to e^- e^+. Two photons fuse by the product in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q):

  \gamma(\varphi) \cdot \gamma(\psi),
  \qquad
  \gamma(\varphi) = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}.

The electron and positron are the braid words

The e^- channel of the product is its coefficient on \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0, which is \varphi_{01}\psi_0 + \varphi_1\psi_{01}: it needs the vertex term \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} of one photon and a single-crossing term of the other. A single crossing \sigma_i is a term of a photon, not a photon, and two bare photons fuse to \gamma(0)\gamma(0) = \mathbf{1}.

prop:gamma-gamma-generates-particles:
Proposition \gamma\gamma production generates the operator basis. Two independent photons multiplied in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q) reach every operator of the six-element basis \{\mathbf{1}, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_-, e^-\}. The photon and the elementary crossings generate the whole particle catalogue through pair production.

Write two colored photons with independent color weights:

  \gamma_1 = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1
             + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1},
  \qquad
  \gamma_2 = \mathbf{1} + \psi_0\sigma_0 + \psi_1\sigma_1
             + \psi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}.

Reduce \gamma_1\cdot\gamma_2 with the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q-q^{-1})\sigma_i + \mathbf{1}. This places five of the six basis operators in the three-term product (where \varphi_{01}=\psi_{01}=0):

\begin{aligned}
  \mathrm{NF}(\gamma_1\gamma_2)
  \;=\;& \underbrace{(1+\varphi_0\psi_0+\varphi_1\psi_1)}_{\mathbf{1}}
  + \underbrace{(\varphi_0+\psi_0+\varphi_0\psi_0\,h)}_{\sigma_0}\sigma_0
  + \underbrace{(\varphi_1+\psi_1+\varphi_1\psi_1\,h)}_{\sigma_1}\sigma_1
  \\[2pt]
  &+ \underbrace{\varphi_0\psi_1}_{L_+}\sigma_0\sigma_1
  + \underbrace{\varphi_1\psi_0}_{L_-}\sigma_1\sigma_0 ,
  \qquad h = q-q^{-1}.
\end{aligned}

The two chiral operators are generated independently. The L_+ coefficient is the cross-color product \varphi_0\psi_1. The L_- coefficient is \varphi_1\psi_0. For any target pair (a,b), the weights (\varphi_0,\varphi_1,\psi_0,\psi_1)=(a,b,1,1) realise L_+=a and L_-=b. The operator L_-=\sigma_1\sigma_0 is absent from any single photon. Since \sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_1 - h\mathbf{1}, the fourth term is \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_0\sigma_1 - h\sigma_0, so the normal-form support of a single photon is contained in \{\mathbf{1},\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\sigma_0\sigma_1\}. The two-photon cross term produces L_-. Restoring the vertex weights \varphi_{01}, \psi_{01} opens the remaining basis operator e^-=\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0, with coefficient \varphi_{01}\psi_0 + \varphi_1\psi_{01}. This completes the basis. The full four-term product, with all six coefficients, is Table 5; its coefficients are polynomials of degree 3 in h.

The span of the two-photon products is all of H_3(q). Each basis word is a linear combination of six explicit products: with P(\varphi;\psi) = \mathrm{NF}(\gamma(\varphi)\gamma(\psi)), \mathbf{1} = P(0;0), \sigma_0 = P(1,0,0;0) - \mathbf{1}, \sigma_1 = P(0,1,0;0) - \mathbf{1}, L_- = P(0,1,0;1,0,0) - \mathbf{1} - \sigma_0 - \sigma_1, L_+ = P(1,0,0;0,1,0) - \mathbf{1} - \sigma_0 - \sigma_1, and e^- = P(0,0,1;1,0,0) - (1-h)\mathbf{1} - (1-h-h^2)\sigma_0 - L_+.
rem:breit-wheeler-pair-production-deriva:
Remark Color-dressed photon, polarization models, and the 4-term Breit--Wheeler normal form. Derivation (Breit--Wheeler categorical pair production).

This derives the Breit--Wheeler categorical pair production with the photon \gamma(\varphi) = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}. It treats the bare photon, the three-term specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0, its polarization limits, and the full four-term product.

Bare photon pair

The bare photon is \gamma(0) = \mathbf{1}, so two bare photons give \gamma(0)\gamma(0) = \mathbf{1}. A bare pair carries no crossing.

By contrast, the single crossing \sigma_0 gives \sigma_0^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_0 + \mathbf{1}, with net valuation 1 + (q - q^{-1}) \approx 1.209 and energy \approx 1.006 MeV; under the photon definition, \sigma_0 is a single colour-plane generator rather than the bare photon \gamma(0) = \mathbf{1}, so \sigma_0^2 evaluates the squared crossing term rather than a bare photon pair.

Colored photon

A photon carries three colour weights:

  \gamma
  = 
  \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1
  {} + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1},

where \varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01} \in R. The generator \sigma_0 acts on the (\sigma, r) plane and \sigma_1 on the (r, g) plane. The fourth term is the chiral pair-production vertex \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_0\sigma_1 - h\,\sigma_0, with h = q - q^{-1} (photon).

This derivation first treats the three-term specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0, which is the same element whether the fourth term is written \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} or \sigma_0\sigma_1. The colour weights were introduced here to match the 2m_e threshold; that is selection against the target, and the weights below are fits.

Normal-form pair product

Expand the product \gamma_1 \cdot \gamma_2 for two 3-term colored photons \gamma_1 = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 and \gamma_2 = \mathbf{1} + \psi_0\sigma_0 + \psi_1\sigma_1. Reduce via \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + \mathbf{1}, where h = q - q^{-1}.

Collecting by basis element yields:

  \mathrm{NF}(\gamma_1 \cdot \gamma_2)
  = 
  \underbrace{(1 + \varphi_0\psi_0 + \varphi_1\psi_1)}_{\gamma}
  \mathbf{1}
  {} + 
  \underbrace{(\varphi_0 + \psi_0 + \varphi_0\psi_0h)}_{\sigma_0}
  \sigma_0
  {} + 
  \underbrace{(\varphi_1 + \psi_1 + \varphi_1\psi_1h)}_{\sigma_1}
  \sigma_1
  {} + 
  \underbrace{\varphi_0\psi_1}_{L_+}
  \sigma_0\sigma_1
  {} + 
  \underbrace{\varphi_1\psi_0}_{L_-}
  \sigma_1\sigma_0.

The Hecke self-energy terms \varphi_0\psi_0 and \varphi_1\psi_1 contribute to the \mathbf{1} coefficient. The terms L_\pm arise strictly from cross-color products \varphi_0\psi_1 and \varphi_1\psi_0.

The net evaluation is the sum of all coefficients:

  \mathrm{net}
  = 
  (1 + \varphi_0 + \varphi_1)(1 + \psi_0 + \psi_1)
  {} + 
  (\varphi_0\psi_0 + \varphi_1\psi_1)h.

Polarization limits

Linear (symmetric) polarization: Take equal color in both generators, \varphi_0 = \varphi_1 = \psi_0 = \psi_1 = \phi.

  • \gamma: 1 + 2\phi^2
  • \sigma_0: 2\phi + \phi^2 h
  • \sigma_1: 2\phi + \phi^2 h
  • L_+: \phi^2
  • L_-: \phi^2

The equal L_\pm content (L_+ = L_- = \phi^2) implies zero chirality. The net valuation is (1 + 2\phi)^2 + 2\phi^2 h. Fitting this to E_{\mathrm{pair}} = 2m_e gives \phi = 0.0487. This value is a fit to the measured electron mass, not a derivation.

Circular (orthogonal) polarization: Take orthogonal polarization, \varphi_0 = s, \varphi_1 = 0, \psi_0 = 0, \psi_1 = s.

  • \gamma: 1
  • \sigma_0: s
  • \sigma_1: s
  • L_+: s^2
  • L_-: 0

Only L_+ appears (L_- = 0). This produces maximally chiral L_\pm content. The Hecke self-energy vanishes (\varphi_0\psi_0 = \varphi_1\psi_1 = 0). The net valuation is (1 + s)^2. Fitting this to E_{\mathrm{pair}} = 2m_e gives s = 0.0978. This value is a fit, not a derivation.

Both fits close the 1.6\% energy gap by construction, so closing it is not evidence for either model. The color weight generates L_\pm content that supplies the missing pair production energy. The asymmetry L_+ \neq L_- in the circular model acts as the categorical expression of photon helicity.

Four-term extension

Activating \varphi_{01} \neq 0 recovers the full photon. The product of two photons spans all six normal-form words. Its e^- (electron-word) coefficient is

  \varphi_{01}\psi_0 + \varphi_1\psi_{01},

so the e^- channel needs the vertex term of one photon and a single-crossing term of the other. For the eigenvalue-pair weights \gamma(0, 0, qh)\,\gamma(0, 0, -q^{-1}h) = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 (Borromean two-photon factorisation) that coefficient is zero. The 6-term normal form is in the \gamma\gamma generation proposition. The coefficients are recomputed exactly over \mathbb{Q}(q).

prop:rj-canonical-inner-product:
Proposition Canonical bilinear form on R(H_r(q)) via Schur orthogonality. The Markov trace on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_r(q) induces a canonical bilinear form on the representation ring R(H_r(q)) via Schur orthogonality. The form is degenerate, and it is an inner product on the span of the two-row classes.

Statement

Let H_r(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra on r strands with parameter q \neq 0, 1. Let R(H_r(q)) = \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash r} \mathbb{Z} \cdot [\lambda] be its representation ring.

(i) The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_r(q) \to \mathbb{Q}(q) uses the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) = q^2/[2]_q. It descends to a bilinear form on R(H_r(q)):

  \langle [\lambda], [\mu] \rangle_{\mathrm{RJ}}
  = 
  d_\lambda(q) \cdot \delta_{\lambda\mu},

where d_\lambda(q) = \prod_{\Box \in \lambda} \frac{[2 + c(\Box)]_q}{[h(\Box)]_q} is the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) quantum dimension of V_\lambda. Here c(\Box) is the content and h(\Box) the hook length (arm + leg + 1) of cell \Box in the Young diagram \lambda, and [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}). The Markov block weights are w_\lambda = \mathrm{tr}_M(p_\lambda) = d_\lambda(q)/[2]_q^{\,r} for a minimal idempotent p_\lambda. Because d_\lambda = 0 whenever \lambda has more than two rows, the form is degenerate: its radical is spanned by the classes [\lambda] with more than two rows, and it is non-degenerate on the span of the two-row classes.

(ii) The form is the one induced by the Markov trace on minimal idempotents:

  \langle [\lambda], [\mu] \rangle_{\mathrm{RJ}}
  =
  [2]_q^{\,r} \, \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(p_\lambda \, p_\mu\bigr)
  =
  d_\lambda(q) \cdot \delta_{\lambda\mu},

which does not depend on the choice of minimal idempotents, since conjugate idempotents have equal trace and p_\lambda p_\mu = 0 for \lambda \neq \mu. Equivalently [2]_q^{\,r}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash r} d_\lambda(q)\, \chi_\lambda(x) for x \in H_r(q). The Markov trace with \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 is unique for a given z, so the form is determined by z alone. Diagonality in the irrep basis does not by itself determine the form: a diagonal form has one free entry for each two-row class, and the normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 fixes only one combination of them.

(iii) Let \gamma = \sigma_1 \cdots \sigma_{r-1}, so that \gamma^r = \Delta^2 is the full twist, which acts on V_\lambda by \theta_\lambda = q^{2 c_\lambda}, where c_\lambda is the content sum of \lambda. For \gcd(r,s) = 1 the torus knot \tau(r,s) is the closure of \gamma^s, and its trace is given by the Rosso–Jones formula:

  [2]_q^{\,r} \, \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\gamma^{s}\bigr)
  =
  \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} (-1)^{j} \, d_{(r-j,1^j)}(q) \, \theta_{(r-j,1^j)}^{\,s/r}
  =
  [r+1]_q \, q^{s(r-1)} - [r-1]_q \, q^{s(r-3)}.

The sum runs over the hooks (r-j, 1^j), and the signs (-1)^j are the coefficients of the Adams operation \psi^r applied to the fundamental representation. Since c_{(r-j,1^j)} = r(r-1-2j)/2, each exponent 2 s c_\lambda / r = s(r-1-2j) is an integer. Only j = 0, 1 contribute, because d_\lambda = 0 for every hook with more than two rows. The unknot-normalised invariant [2]_q^{\,r-1} \, q^{-2s(r-1)} \, \mathrm{tr}_M(\gamma^s) is the Jones polynomial of \tau(r,s) at t = q^{-2}.
prf:rj-canonical-inner-product:
Proof Proof of rj canonical inner product. (i) The Markov trace factors through the Grothendieck ring: \mathrm{tr}_M(a) = \sum_\lambda d_\lambda(q) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_\lambda(a), where \mathrm{tr}_\lambda is the character of irrep \lambda, up to the factor [2]_q^{-r} that converts d_\lambda into the block weight w_\lambda. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the framing ratio is z/(z - (q - q^{-1})) = q^4, which collapses each Ocneanu numerator into a quantum integer and gives w_\lambda = d_\lambda(q)/[2]_q^{\,r} with d_\lambda the \mathfrak{sl}_2 hook-content dimension (Markov parameter reconciliation). Restricting to the class functions, spanned by \{\chi_\lambda\}, gives the stated diagonal form.

(ii) The irreps \{\chi_\lambda : \lambda \vdash r\} form an orthogonal basis of the center Z(H_r(q)) under the Markov trace pairing. Schur orthogonality \mathrm{tr}_M(\chi_\lambda \chi_\mu) = d_\lambda \delta_{\lambda\mu} follows from the semisimplicity of H_r(q) for generic q [rosso-jones1993]; the classes with more than two rows have d_\lambda = 0 and lie in the radical. Any other bilinear form diagonal in \{\chi_\lambda\} and normalized at the identity differs only by rescaling the Markov parameter z.

(iii) The Rosso–Jones formula [rosso-jones1993] decomposes J(\tau(r,s)) over irreps of H_r(q). Each irrep contributes its quantum dimension d_\lambda(q) multiplied by the s-th power of its full-twist eigenvalue \omega_\lambda. This provides the inner product \langle \omega^s, [\mathrm{triv}] \rangle_{\mathrm{RJ}}, where [\mathrm{triv}] denotes the class of the trivial representation in R(H_r(q)). \square
prop:knot-operator-selection:
Proposition Knot operator selection via Frobenius dual. Proposition (knot operator selection). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a QOU with archimedean realisation H_r(q). Let \{\tau(r_i, s_i)\}_{i=1}^{6} be the embeddable torus knots on \Sigma_4. Let \gamma_1, \gamma_2 \in H_3(q) be two incoming particle states.

(i) Spectral decomposition of the mediating endomorphism. The Lagrangian endomorphism \Phi decomposes via Schur orthogonality:

  \Phi
  =
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash r}
  d_\lambda(q) \cdot \Phi_\lambda,

where d_\lambda(q) is the quantum dimension of irrep \lambda. The operator \Phi_\lambda = e_\lambda \Phi e_\lambda is the projection of \Phi onto the \lambda-isotypic component. Each irrep \lambda corresponds to a torus knot \tau(r,s) via the knot eigenbasis.

(ii) Multi-channel pair production. The categorical action of two photons \gamma_1, \gamma_2 through the mediating endomorphism is:

  \mathcal{S}(\gamma_1, \gamma_2)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}\!\left(
    \Phi \cdot (\gamma_1 \otimes \gamma_2)
  \right)
  =
  \sum_{\lambda}
  d_\lambda(q) \cdot
  \mathrm{tr}_\lambda\!\bigl(
    \gamma_1 \cdot \beta(\tau_\lambda) \cdot \gamma_2
  \bigr).

Multiple knot operators act simultaneously, each weighted by its quantum dimension; the interaction is a superposition of channels.

(iii) Frobenius demand--supply pairing. The Frobenius self-duality A \xrightarrow{\sim} A^\vee via \int_A \circ \mu identifies the normal form decomposition of each state with its dual. For a state K = \sum_i c_i b_i in the basis \{b_i\} = \{\gamma, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_-, e^-\}: positive coefficients c_i > 0 are supply (channels the state provides) and negative coefficients c_i < 0 are demand (channels the state requires from its partner). The Frobenius pairing \langle K_1, K_2 \rangle_F = \mathrm{tr}_M(K_1 \cdot K_2) is degenerate on H_3(q) under the canonical Markov convention: its radical is the one-dimensional span of the q-antisymmetriser v = (-q^3, q^2, q^2, -q, -q, 1), and \det G = 0 identically in q. The pairing therefore descends to a non-degenerate pairing on the quotient H_3(q)/\mathrm{rad}, and a minimal-norm supply exists there and is unique modulo the radical — but only for demand profiles lying in the image of the pairing, equivalently those orthogonal to v. A demand profile with nonzero radical component admits no supply at all.

(iv) Minimum-action selection. The physical interaction selects the \Phi \in \mathrm{End}(A) minimizing the categorical action |\mathfrak{S}| = |\mathrm{tr}(\Phi)| among those compatible with the on-shell condition \star_q F_\nabla = F_\nabla. The dominant channel is the irrep \lambda_* with the largest |d_{\lambda_*}(q) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{\lambda_*}(\gamma_1 \cdot \beta(\tau_{\lambda_*}) \cdot \gamma_2)|.
prf:knot-operator-selection:
Proof Proof of knot operator selection. Sketch.

(i) The Hecke algebra H_r(q) is semisimple for generic q, so \mathrm{End}_{H_r(q)}(V^{\otimes r}) decomposes as \bigoplus_\lambda \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda) by the Wedderburn theorem. The Markov trace projects onto each component with weight d_\lambda(q) by Schur orthogonality (RJ inner product).

(ii) The categorical action \mathfrak{S} = \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes \Phi) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A = \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) is linear in \Phi. Substituting the spectral decomposition (i) and using the identification \mathrm{tr} = \mathrm{tr}_M (archimedean descent) gives the stated sum over channels.

(iii) The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_F = \int_A \mu(a \otimes b) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\hat\beta_a) \cdot \rho(\hat\beta_b)) is the categorical inner product. Non-degeneracy (QUO-1) means every element has a unique Frobenius dual. In the NF basis, this identifies positive coefficients with morphisms \mathbf{1} \to A (supply, via coevaluation) and negative coefficients with morphisms A \to \mathbf{1} (demand, via evaluation).

(iv) The on-shell condition constrains \Phi to lie in the self-dual curvature subspace (S([\sigma_i, \sigma_j])^* = [\sigma_i, \sigma_j]). Within this subspace, the extremum of |\mathrm{tr}(\Phi)| is attained at the irrep with largest quantum dimension times character evaluation. For pair production at the observed q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps), this is T_{2,3} (trefoil, e^-) — the lowest-crossing operator that unconditionally opens the degree-3 channel.

Explicit dual construction

Consider a state K \in H_3(q) with decomposition K = \sum_i c_i b_i. The Frobenius dual K^\vee is the unique element satisfying

  \langle K^\vee, b_i \rangle_F = c_i
  \quad \forall i.

By non-degeneracy (read on the quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, where the induced pairing is non-degenerate; on H_n itself \det G = 0 exactly, the (1^3) block being the radical), K^\vee exists and is unique. In the basis, K^\vee = \sum_i c_i (G^{-1})_{ij} b_j, where G_{ij} = \langle b_i, b_j \rangle_F = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) is the 6 \times 6 Gram matrix of H_3(q).

The demand vector of K is the negative part:

  \mathrm{dem}(K) = \sum_{i : c_i < 0} |c_i| \, b_i^\vee.

The operator that fills the demand at minimum crossing energy is

  \Phi_{\mathrm{min}}
  =
  \arg\min_{\Phi \in \mathrm{End}(A)_{\mathrm{on-shell}}}
  \left\{
    \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\Phi)
    \ \Big|\ 
    \langle \Phi, \mathrm{dem}(K) \rangle_F \geq
    \|\mathrm{dem}(K)\|_F
  \right\}.

For the positron (e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}), the demand profile is \{-0.218\gamma, -0.209 L_+, -0.209 L_-\}. The positron word demands vacuum energy and L_\pm content. The minimum-energy supply is the coevaluation \mathrm{coev}_A \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A^\vee, which provides exactly the identity and Hopf content from the rigid structure. Its cost is \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \approx 2.011.
rem:knot-operator-selection-multichannel:
Remark Multi-channel interpretation of knot operator selection. The Lagrangian endomorphism \Phi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) of the categorical action decomposes over the irreducible representations of H_n(q). This decomposition and the Frobenius self-duality A \cong A^\vee determine the specific knot operators that mediate any interaction and their corresponding weights.

Multi-channel interpretation

For Breit--Wheeler pair production \gamma\gamma \to e^-e^+, the full interaction is

  \mathcal{S}(\gamma_1, \gamma_2)
  =
  \underbrace{d_{\mathrm{triv}}(q) \cdot P_{T_{1,0}}}_{\text{elastic: polarisation change}}
  +
  \underbrace{d_{\Box}(q) \cdot P_{T_{2,1}}}_{\text{single crossing}}
  +
  \underbrace{d_{\Box\Box}(q) \cdot P_{T_{2,2}}}_{\text{Hopf link (gluon)}}
  +
  \underbrace{d_{\yng(2,1)}(q) \cdot P_{T_{2,3}}}_{\text{trefoil}}
  +  \cdots

All channels fire simultaneously. Two incoming photons can:

  • change polarisation (trivial operator, no pair created),
  • exchange a gluon (T_{2,2}, Hopf link),
  • pass through the trefoil operator T_{2,3}; under the electron ruling (electron) the e^-e^+ pair is read from the \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 coefficient (Breit--Wheeler pair production), not from this channel,
  • pass through the cinquefoil operator T_{2,5}, suppressed by higher crossing energy; the muon word is not ruled, so this is not yet a \mu^-\mu^+ channel.

These events occur in a single interaction. The quantum dimension d_\lambda(q) weights each channel. The branching ratios depend entirely on q and the incoming photon polarisation content \varphi_0, \varphi_1.

Experiments detect the dominant channel, which carries the largest weight. The subdominant channels contribute to radiative corrections, vacuum polarisation, and the running of coupling constants. The elastic channel (T_{1,0}) is always present: photon--photon scattering without pair creation is the leading process, and pair creation is a threshold-activated subdominant channel.
prose:intro-mesons-nucleons:
Once quark–antiquark pairs are generated at a Hecke vertex, colour confinement restricts observable states to closed links whose total colour holonomy is trivial. The simplest composite state is a meson, formed by a quark strand and an antiquark strand joined into a two-component link along a single colour tube.

Forming a baryon requires three quark strands. Rather than linking pairwise, the three strands close into the Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3—a Brunnian link in which every two-component sublink is trivial yet the three-component closure is topologically inseparable. This section defines the meson formation chain and proves the existence of the categorical proton as the minimal-action Borromean closure bounded by the hadronic scale \mathfrak{E}_0.
rem:meson-formation-chain:
Remark The meson formation chain. The meson arises through a three-step formation chain.

Step 1: Pair production. A 1.6\% energy gap separates the bare photon pair from the threshold 2\mathfrak{m}_e. The color weights \varphi_0, \varphi_1 close this gap by supplying Hopf link terms. Two colored photons \gamma_i = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} thus fuse into an electron--positron pair:

  \gamma_1 \cdot \gamma_2
   \longrightarrow 
  e^- + e^+
  +  \text{\(L_\pm\) content}(L_+ = \varphi_0\psi_1, L_- = \varphi_1\psi_0)

Step 2: Quark creation. To create a quark on the e^- channel, L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1 from the colored photon normal form acts as a creation operator:

  L_+ \cdot e^-
  = 
  (\sigma_0\sigma_1)(\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0)
  \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NF}}
  \mathfrak{u} + \varphi_0\psi_1\cdot e^-

Two independent pair productions create two quark--antiquark channels: \mathfrak{u} + \bar{\mathfrak{u}} and \mathfrak{d} + \bar{\mathfrak{d}}.

Step 3: Meson binding. To form the meson, a quark from one production binds with an antiquark from the other. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H mediates this binding:

  \mathfrak{u} + \bar{\mathfrak{d}}
  \xrightarrow{\mathcal{L}_H}
  \mathfrak{M}_+
  = 
  T_{01} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H \cdot T_{10}

Summary chain.

  \gamma\gamma
  \xrightarrow{\text{Breit--Wheeler}}
  e^- e^+
  \xrightarrow{L_+}
  q\bar{q}
  \xrightarrow{\mathcal{L}_H}
  \mathfrak{M}

Each arrow is a morphism in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q). Breit--Wheeler multiplies by \sigma_0^2. Quark creation left-multiplies by L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1. Meson binding inserts \mathcal{L}_H = \sigma_0\sigma_1 between the quark and antiquark crossing pairs. Evaluating at q = q_0 yields the meson normal form:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{M}_+)
  = 
  +0.209\sigma_1
  +  1.044 L_+
  +  0.044 L_-
  +  0.218 e^-

This produces the net value \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{M}_+) = +1.515.

prop:categorical-proton-exists:
Proposition Existence of the categorical proton. The categorical proton exists as a well-defined element of the Hecke algebra H_3(q):

\mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) \in H_3(q).

It satisfies Frobenius stability G x[\gamma] \ge 0 at every step of the LP reduction.

Archimedean specialisation. The underlying categorical identities hold over an abstract coefficient ring. Their archimedean realisation requires real- or complex-analytic constructs. What follows invokes these constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. What follows therefore sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall.
prf:categorical-proton-exists: Proof Proof of existence of the categorical proton. The Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0 \sigma_1^{-1})^3 is a concrete element of the braid group B_3, and thus of the Hecke algebra H_3(q) via the standard representation. Typed crossings for the partition (\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) and the gluon stabiliser L_- = \sigma_1 \sigma_0 are likewise elements of H_3(q). Their product reduces via Gröbner--Shirshov to a canonical Hecke normal form. LP-dual feasibility verifies the non-negativity constraint G x[\gamma] \ge 0 at every intermediate step. Consequently, the categorical proton \mathfrak{p} exists as a well-defined, LP-stable element.
sec:mesons-nucleons-categorical-proton-u: Within the three-strand Borromean link topology, the orientation of the internal trefoil twist distinguishes the two nucleon isospin states. This section proves the uniqueness of the categorical proton and categorical neutron in H_3(q), constructs the meson-to-proton Borromean lifting morphism, and demonstrates that crossing reversal \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1} maps particles to antiparticles while exchanging left- and right-handed trefoil chirality between the electron and positron.
prop:categorical-proton-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the categorical proton up to braid isotopy. The triple (\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) and the Borromean braiding pattern \mathcal{B}_3 uniquely determine the categorical proton \mathfrak{p} up to braid isotopy:

\mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) \in H_3(q).

Its Hecke normal form in H_3(q) is unique, and the S_3 permutation symmetry on the color tubes ensures independence from position assignments.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0.
